content.text:
I found nothing to flag in the document. Every claim traces to the record, and the one went_wrong item is not something that field excludes.

- **Root cause:** It is said as Code-Fix's reading of the source, which nothing ran, and the document calls it unverified. So it stands as a reading.
- **Second contributing factor (no staged rollout):** The 18:15 mix of off and on evaluations falls in the minute the flag was switched on. Every evaluation from the next minute on came back on, so "every evaluation came back on" holds.
- **First contributing factor (no test for this case):** This is the closest call. Code-Fix never says outright that the existing tests missed this case. It does say the crash was always there for this input and that both new tests would fail against the old code, so I counted the claim as supported.
- **went_wrong:** The item says the second candidate (C2) was marked refuted on the test run for the first (C1). The fourth contributing factor only says switching the flag off didn't reach the service. Saying the refutation itself was unsound is a different lesson from the same facts, not a repeat. It isn't one of the excluded kinds either: not something left on purpose, not a limit of the record, not about Code-Fix's revision.

Not judged: the action items, the "stops the harm" steps and the what-if parts of the "had it been otherwise" lines. I did check what those lines say actually happened, such as the revert not taking effect.

supported.quote: The monthly path that monthly-spend-feature switches on works out a shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing the month's total by the number of purchases made this month. Nothing guards against that number being zero, so for every shopper who has bought before but not this month, line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
An admin switched on a new feature that sent shoppers' account pages through a monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely fails for anyone who has bought nothing so far this month.

With monthly-spend-feature back on, account pages could keep failing for every shopper who has bought nothing this month, and switching the flag off in the flag provider might again not change what io-shop evaluates.
Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after it was switched off in the flag provider at {P2.1}
Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, starting in the onset minute and continuing through the last minute read.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors appear in io-shop's logs from the onset minute onwards and not before it.

An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. In that same minute, flag evaluations started moving from off to on, and from the next minute every evaluation came back on, which sent account page requests down the flag's monthly path.

The revision running on every replica, which the history does not name. With it in place and the flag off, account pages rendered normally and the flag evaluated off in every minute read before the onset.
The monthly path likely divides by the number of purchases made this month, which is zero for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

No check was seen that exercised the monthly path behind monthly-spend-feature for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. By Code-Fix's reading, the tests in the file it read did not cover that case.
No staged rollout of the flag was seen. From the minute after it was switched on, every evaluation of monthly-spend-feature in io-shop came back on.
The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
